name: Familial Multiple Trichoepithelioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnosis of Familial Multiple Trichoepithelioma

criteria.description: Positive family history of multiple trichoepitheliomas with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Presence of multiple, small, skin-colored papules or nodules predominantly on the face, especially nasolabial folds and forehead
Histological confirmation showing basaloid cell nests with follicular differentiation consistent with trichoepithelioma
Identification of pathogenic variants in the CYLD gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple characteristic facial lesions with positive family history and histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

other: Histopathology showing basaloid tumor islands with follicular differentiation

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology showing infiltrative basal cell carcinoma
Lack of family history typical for trichoepithelioma
Presence of multiple adnexal tumors including cylindromas and spiradenomas
More extensive tumor types beyond trichoepitheliomas
Genetic overlap but broader clinical spectrum

redFlags: Rapid growth or ulceration of lesions suggesting malignant transformation
Family history of multiple adnexal tumors or skin cancers
Development of lesions outside typical facial distribution
references: OMIM Entry - Familial Multiple Trichoepithelioma, OMIM #601622
Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
